lines.text: At 3:12 last night, my doorbell camera sent me an alert: *Person detected.* I opened the clip. My porch was empty.
Except for the little box the camera draws around a person. The box was there. *Around nothing.*
These cameras don't see ghosts. They run a program that looks for the shape of a body. Head, shoulders, legs. When it finds one, it draws a box.
So I watched the whole clip. The box stood on my porch for six minutes. Then it walked to my door.
The next night, three alerts. *Driveway. Front door.* And then a camera I'd forgotten I even had.
I went through it frame by frame. Every frame, the box was a little closer to the camera. To my bedroom door.
And then it got a name.
My camera learns the faces of the people who live here, so it can tell family from strangers. I live alone.
Last night it saved a new face. The photo is an empty box. And it labeled it *with my name.*
This morning I walked into my kitchen, and my phone buzzed.
The clip shows me, in a red box. And at the table, in my chair, there's a green box. With my name on it.
My house thinks I'm the stranger now.
